The 2026 Ballon d'Or nominees have been announced as the best male and female footballers of the year are identified. Harry Kane is among those in the running for the men's prize and is the bookmakers' favourite to be crowned. Kane scored 73 goals last season, enjoying one of the best campaigns of his career and he could become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001. Kane is joined the 30-man long-list by international teammates Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice. messages.text: Sabalenka survives Noskova battle to keep US Open three-peat bid alive

metadata.summary: Aryna Sabalenka maintained her hopes of a third successive US Open title with a three-set victory over Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in an absorbing quarter-final - a result that retains her status as world No 1 for at least one more day.
metadata.content: US Open 2026: Aryna Sabalenka edges into semi-finals with three-set win over Linda Noskova in thriller | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open 2026: Aryna Sabalenka edges into semi-finals with three-set win over Linda Noskova in thriller Aryna Sabalenka retains world No 1 spot with battling win - but will lose it on Wednesday if Elena Rybakina reaches semi-finals; Sabalenka is looking to become first woman to win US Open three times in row since Serena Williams between 2012 and 2014; watch tournament live on Sky Sports Tuesday 8 September 2026 19:41, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the US Open Open Quarter-final match between Aryna Sabalenka and Linda Noskova. Aryna Sabalenka maintained her hopes of a third successive US Open title with a three-set victory over Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in an absorbing quarter-final - a result that retains her status as world No 1 for at least one more day. The 28-year-old beat Noskova 7-6 (7-1) 3-6 7-6 (10-7), coming through two tie-breaks - and a 4-2 deficit in the final set - as she sealed victory with a second-serve ace to set up a meeting with the winner of Tuesday night's all-American clash between Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro in the semi-finals. messages.text: Ferrari vow to come back stronger after Monza 'failure'

metadata.summary: Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur says his team will head to this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid with "all the energy" to bounce back from their "failure" at Monza.
metadata.content: Spanish GP: Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur says team will come back stronger in Madrid after Italian GP 'failure' at Monza | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Spanish GP: Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur says team will come back stronger in Madrid after Italian GP 'failure' at Monza Ferrari scored just eight points last time out in Monza on a weekend they hoped Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc could fight for the win; watch every session of the Spanish Grand Prix at a new track in Madrid from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Tuesday 8 September 2026 11:51, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch back the 360-degree angle of Ferrari's Charles Leclerc's crash at the Italian Grand Prix Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur says his team will head to this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid with "all the energy" to bounce back from their "failure" at Monza. There were big expectations for Ferrari at their home event after Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were quick in Friday practice, only to miss out on the front row in qualifying before a dismal race on Sunday. Hamilton dropped from fourth to 10th after going side by side with Leclerc at the first chicane, going through the gravel at Turn 2, which he was unhappy with. But, after a disappointing start to the new campaign, how will they handle the challenge of juggling three games per week? And has their rebuild neglected one key part of their squad? From 40 games to 60? messages.text: Team USA play down injury fears and ready to take down 'tough' Europe

metadata.summary: Team USA captain Angela Stanford insists Angel Yin will be fit to feature against Team Europe this week at the Solheim Cup and has backed her side to claim away victory in the Netherlands.
metadata.content: Solheim Cup 2026: Team USA play down fitness concern over Angel Yin and relish chance to take down' tough' Team Europe | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Solheim Cup 2026: Team USA play down fitness concern over Angel Yin and relish chance to take down' tough' Team Europe Angel Yin has only made one start on the LPGA Tour since withdrawing from the KPMG Women's PGA Championship in June with a stomach issue; Yin features for Team USA at Bernardus Golf, where they look to regain the trophy; watch live from 6am on Friday on Sky Sports Golf By Ali Stafford at Bernardus Golf Tuesday 8 September 2026 17:32, UK Image: Team USA captain Angela Stanford looks to secure a rare away victory in Europe and retain the Solheim Cup Team USA captain Angela Stanford insists Angel Yin will be fit to feature against Team Europe this week at the Solheim Cup and has backed her side to claim away victory in the Netherlands. Yin has not completed a 72-hole tournament since May, having missed the cut at the US Women's Open in June before withdrawing mid-tournament from the KPMG Women's PGA Championship later that month due to illness. The two-time LPGA Tour winner qualified second in the US Solheim Cup points list despite missing the final two majors of the season with the undisclosed stomach issue, which saw her lose around 2.5 stone in weight.
